newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian bourse launched in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian bourse launched in West Bank.

text.p: The first Palestinian stock market opened on Tuesday in the West Bank town of Nablus, officials said.
"The market has opened," Safwan Bataina, general manager of the Palestine Securities Exchange (PSE), told reporters.
In initial trading, 100 shares of the Arab Insurance Company changed hands for four Jordanian dinars each, and 10 shares of Arab Real Estate were sold for 11 dinars each.
Bourse officials have said the PSE would be launched with one trading session per week, adding more weekly sessions as trading volume dictated.
The PSE said on Monday that 23 companies had been listed on the exchange and 20 other companies were expected to complete listing procedures by the end of the one-month introductory phase.
It said that 60 public share-holding companies were eligible to be listed with an estimated capitalisation of $700 million.
The exchange has signed an agreement with the Jordan-based Arab Bank to act as a clearing house.
